framework: IEEE 3129-2023 IEEE Standard for Robustness Testing and Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Image Recognition Service
requirement_paraphrase: The catalogue description says the standard provides test specifications and indicators for common corruption and adversarial attacks, describes robustness attack threats, and sets out an assessment framework to evaluate robustness of image recognition services under varied settings.
what_is_tested: Robustness of AI based image recognition services against common corruption and adversarial attacks

framework: ETSI TS 104 275 V1.1.1 Securing Artificial Intelligence (SAI); Application of Baseline Cyber Security Requirements principles to Generative AI; Preventing Harm from Deepfakes
requirement_paraphrase: Annex C gives conformance test cases, each with a test purpose, method and pass or fail verdict, for several principle clauses (for example C.2.3.2 pre-deployment risk assessment, p. 22-23). The summary reported no test case for Principle 9.
what_is_tested: Conformance with the principles' provisions, including pre-deployment risk assessment

framework: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems (G7; date not stated in the text received)
requirement_paraphrase: Organizations should monitor for vulnerabilities, incidents, emerging risks and misuse after deployment and act on what they find.

framework: Draft Framework Convention on artificial intelligence, human rights, democracy and the rule of law, CM(2024)52-prov1 (Ministers' Deputies, 15 March 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Risk and impact management measures should, where appropriate, require testing of AI systems before they are first made available and when significantly modified.
what_is_tested: AI systems, impacts on human rights, democracy and the rule of law
who_tests: Not specified (to be set by each Party's measures)

framework: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development: Guiding Principles (Health Canada page, published 27 October 2021, last modified 29 July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Training and test datasets should be appropriately independent, with patient, data acquisition and site factors considered.

framework: DoD Directive 3000.09, Autonomy in Weapon Systems (reissued 25 January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems must pass rigorous hardware and software verification and validation and realistic developmental and operational test and evaluation; systems with AI capabilities get the same rigorous developmental and operational T&E. Systems must function as expected in realistic operational environments against adaptive adversaries.
what_is_tested: Weapon system hardware, software and AI capability behaviour in realistic operational conditions, including against adaptive adversaries
who_tests: DoD components (developers and test organisations; DOT&E oversees operational T&E standards and approves test plans, Sec. 2.5)

framework: SR 26-2, Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (issued 17 April 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Model testing is a core part of development; it can include out-of-sample and out-of-time testing, comparison of alternative assumptions and assessment of data quality, with rigour matched to complexity and materiality.
what_is_tested: Model accuracy on held out data and time periods, data quality, sensitivity to assumptions
who_tests: Model developers at the banking organisation

framework: Texas H.B. 149, Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (Senate Committee Report version, committee substitute)
requirement_paraphrase: The department must create a regulatory sandbox where an approved person can test an AI system for a limited time and on a limited basis without a licence or other authorisation, for up to 36 months.
what_is_tested: Limited real-world testing of AI systems under regulator approval
who_tests: Sandbox participants, with department and agency approval

framework: Good machine learning practice for medical device development: guiding principles (MHRA, FDA, Health Canada; GOV.UK page showing 'Updated 5 October 2026', first published 27 October 2021)
clause_or_page: Guiding principle 6 (Model design is tailored to the available data and reflects the intended use of the device)
requirement_paraphrase: Model design should support mitigation of known risks such as overfitting, performance degradation and security risks, and clinical benefits and risks should inform the performance goals used for testing.
what_is_tested: Performance goals derived from clinical benefit and risk; mitigation of overfitting and degradation

framework: APRA letter to industry on artificial intelligence (AI), dated April 2026 per page
clause_or_page: Observations for Executive Management, 'Traditional change management and assurance is in place but is not sufficient for dynamic AI solutions', expectations list, final bullet
requirement_paraphrase: APRA expects regulated entities to conduct comprehensive risk and information security assessments prior to deployment and throughout the lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Risk and information security of AI solutions before deployment and across the lifecycle

framework: Guidelines on Ensuring Safety of Automated Driving Vehicles (自動運転車の安全確保に関するガイドライン), 2nd edition, revised 30 September 2025 (original 7 June 2024), MLIT
requirement_paraphrase: Scenario based safety evaluation: created scenarios and test cases are checked for conformity through simulation, test track driving and real traffic environment testing.
what_is_tested: Conformity of the vehicle with scenario test cases
who_tests: Vehicle manufacturer or developer (actor not confirmed in the text read)

framework: Regulatory Guidelines for Software Medical Devices: A Life Cycle Approach, GL-04-R2, Revision 2.0, April 2022, HSA
requirement_paraphrase: The registration file for an AI medical device should include a test protocol and test report covering verification and validation against the performance specification, including acceptance limits and anomalies; performance claims such as sensitivity and specificity must be backed by these reports.
what_is_tested: Verification and validation of the AI medical device against its performance specification

framework: Guidelines for Financial Institutions Adopting Enabling Technologies, issued 15/11/2021, status shown as In-Force on the CBUAE Rulebook page
requirement_paraphrase: Where relevant, institutions should carry out rigorous, independent validation and testing of material trained models before deployment, by an internal independent function or an external organisation; models should be checked for unintuitive or false causal relationships.
what_is_tested: Material trained Big Data Analytics and AI models
who_tests: Internal independent function or external organisation
